market_holds: Sealed baseline (2026-11-10 18:11 UTC): spot 5.63, front-expiry (Nov 13) straddle 14.2%, event-implied move 13.6%, 25d skew +14.6 vol points (downside paid) with put/call OI 0.29; run-up -7.1% over 5d and -3.9% over 20d; 70.8% below the 52-week high and 6% above the low. Prior prints moved -21.0%, -12.4%, +13.7%, -10.1% (median |move| 13.0%), so the options price the usual reaction. Yahoo daily bars show the stock ran from 5.78 (Oct 30) to 6.59 (Nov 4) and gave it all back to about 5.57 by Nov 10 (-15%), across Live Nation's Nov 5 release (secondary GTV flat, concert resale lower) and Vivid Seats' print and debt-to-equity recap (SEAT 2.74 to 1.50). The read-through from peers is therefore already in the price. Consensus Q3 (Chartmill/FXEmpire, read 2026-11-10): revenue about $524-528M, EPS $0.10-0.11, revenue estimate cut 7.8% over three months. BofA (Underperform, Aug 2026) models Q3 GMS at $2.46B, against $2.43B a year earlier. Guide from Aug 12: FY26 GMS $10.1-10.3B, which with H1 at $5.34B implies H2 of $4.76-4.96B, -1% to +3% against H2 2025's $4.8B (management said low single digits). FY adjusted EBITDA $400-420M, which implies H2 of $222-242M against $130.5M in H2 2025, +70% to +86%. Short interest about 30.7M shares (FINRA, Jul 31 2026; about 9% of shares outstanding, more of the float) with 6.2 days to cover. Sell side split: Citi upgraded to Buy on Sep 18 (target $7) expecting a Q3 EBITDA beat; BofA Underperform; consensus Hold, average target about $10.
view: This print will trade on two lines. The first is whether management holds the FY adjusted EBITDA guide of $400-420M, which needs H2 EBITDA up roughly 70-85% on flat GMS. The second is any Q4 or 2027 framing: MLB labour risk, regulation, and a concert-resale squeeze from Ticketmaster. Q3 GMS growth matters less. The independent Q3 data are flat for the category. Live Nation (Nov 5) says secondary GTV was flat, with sports up and concert resale down because Ticketmaster is constraining scalpers. Vivid Seats grew marketplace GOV 1% on a comp that was down 29%. That agrees with StubHub's own low-single-digit H2 guide and BofA's $2.46B, so I see no GMS surprise the price misses. Two things could make Q3 GMS come in below that. July World Cup cancellations are netted out of GMS, and there was fulfillment and legal fallout after the tournament. Q3 2025 also had late-September tour onsales pulled into it, which BofA flagged at the time. Both were public and are probably in the 7.8% cut to revenue estimates. On EBITDA, the case for an upside surprise is real but unproven: Citi expects a Q3 beat, World Cup support costs are gone, and gross margin should return to the mid-80s. Management reaffirmed the guide in August knowing July, and that the guide already includes the World Cup support and regulatory costs. On the other side are the stage's history of disappointing on costs (Q2 adjusted EPS $0.02 against $0.07 expected), BofA's view that the World Cup pulled demand forward, and a credibility discount after three post-print falls of 10-21%. The setup is two-sided. The stock is at about 7x guided EBITDA, 31% below its post-Q2 close, short interest is elevated and calls dominate open interest, so a held guide could squeeze. A trimmed EBITDA guide or a cautious 2027 tone would extend the pattern. I found no dated in-quarter evidence that StubHub's own Q3 diverges from the flat category, and none that settles the margin question. My lean is slightly negative, because the company's record at prints is poor and the concert-resale headwind is structural, but it is close to a coin flip.

recommendation.reason: The peer data (Live Nation secondary flat, Vivid Seats GOV +1%) match management's low-single-digit H2 GMS guide and the 7.8% cut to revenue estimates, and the stock already fell about 15% across those peer prints. The deciding line is whether the steep H2 EBITDA ramp holds. I found no public, dated evidence that settles it either way, and the options already price a 13.6% move with downside skew. With no mechanism the price lacks, I make no call.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 adjusted EBITDA well above about $110M with the $400-420M guide held or raised, plus a buyback (FCF and the October refinancing allow one), would make the elevated short interest a squeeze and argue up. A cut to the EBITDA guide or Q3 GMS below $2.4B would argue down.

self_critique: The strongest case against a near-50 view is that it is too passive in both directions. For up: the stock is at about 7x guided EBITDA and 31% below its post-Q2 close, estimates were already cut, short interest is high, and Citi expects an EBITDA beat. Simply holding the guide could produce a double-digit squeeze, and my mild negative tilt rests largely on the 'stock falls after prints' pattern, which is extrapolating the last reactions (a bias the playbook names). For down: the guide needs an extraordinary H2 margin step-up. Concert resale is being structurally constrained by Ticketmaster, and World Cup cancellations and legal costs could have leaked into Q3. A company that has missed cost expectations before could trim the EBITDA guide. Either case could be right, which is the reason not to recommend.
